newsitem.title: USA: Wyser-Pratte wins support in Wallace proxy fight.
newsitem.headline: Wyser-Pratte wins support in Wallace proxy fight.

text.p: Wyser-Pratte and Co said on Friday another independent advisory firm had endorsed it in its proxy fight against Wallace Computer Services Inc.

The New York-based Proxy Monitor published a report recommending Wallace shareholders support the three Wyser-Pratte director-nominees and both the tender offer by-law proposal and the business combination statute proposal, Wyser-Pratte said.
Wyser-Pratte filed proxy materials with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission seeking to have three directors elected to Wallace's board.
Wyser-Pratte has also tried to pass a proposal for Wallace to opt out of a Delaware by-law, Section 203, which would make it easier for a potential acquisitor to purchase the company.

Finally, Wyser-Pratte said it has proposed an amendment to prohibit Wallace's board to continue allegedly defensive measures against a takeover beyond 90 days after an initial, qualified offer without obtaining stockholder approval.
Wallace has called the amendment invalid.

"We believe the Wallace board stands in need of more individuals not only mindful of who owns the company but also aware of the fiduciary role played by corporate directors," Wyser-Pratte quoted The Proxy Monitor as saying.
Wallace was not immediately available to comment further.
